chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad and Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, altogether, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Muhammad ibn Humran, who said:

Ismail, son of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), fell sick, so Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said to him: 'Say, "O Lord, O Lord" ten times, for whoever says that will be called out: "At your service! What is your need?".'

key_terms.أَبُو عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdullah (AS), referring to Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS)
key_terms.إِسْمَاعِيلُ بْنُ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Ismail ibn Abi Abdullah (AS), a prominent companion of the Imams
key_terms.لَبَّيْكَ: At your service / I respond to your call
key_terms.يَا رَبِّ: O Lord, a form of direct address to God

ai.seo_question: What specific supplication did Imam Sadiq (AS) recommend for illness?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (AS) prescribes a specific dhikr for Ismail ibn Abi Abdullah (AS) during illness, highlighting the Shia emphasis on the intercessory power of invoking the Lord's name with urgency. The divine response, 'Labbayk' (At your service), signifies immediate acceptance and readiness to fulfill the supplicant's need, reinforcing the concept of *Istijabah* (answering prayers) in times of distress. This practice underscores the spiritual intimacy between the believer and Allah, where simple, repeated invocation serves as a key to divine mercy and healing.
